title: Quasi-coherent higher direct images vanish above proper fibre dimension
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $d\geq0$ be an integer. Suppose every scheme-theoretic fibre $X_y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has Krull dimension at most $d$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ [pqf-def-coherent], one has $R^if_*F=0$ for every $i>d$, where higher direct images are those of structure-sheaf modules [def-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-direct-image]. No Noetherian or flatness assumption is required.

source.place: Tag 0E7D, lemma-higher-direct-images-zero-above-dimension-fibre, part (1), at each point of Y; arbitrary-base statement. Compare the Noetherian predecessor coherent.tex Tag 02V7.

proof.text: Work locally on the target. For an affine open $V\subset Y$, put $X_V=f^{-1}V$ and restrict $F$ to $X_V$. The restricted morphism is proper by base change, its fibres are the original fibres, and the restricted module is quasi-coherent by pullback. Higher direct images restrict to the higher direct images of this restricted morphism. Consequently it suffices to prove the assertion with $Y$ affine. A proper morphism is quasi-compact by finite type and quasi-separated by separatedness. For such a morphism, $R^pf_*F$ is quasi-coherent and its sections over the affine target identify with $H^p(X,F)$. The affine tilde/Gamma counit identifies $R^pf_*F$ with the sheaf associated to these sections. It therefore suffices to show $H^p(X,F)=0$ for $p>d$.

source.place: Tag 0E7D, lemma-higher-direct-images-zero-above-dimension-fibre, affine-local reduction and third paragraph

proof.text: Keep $Y$ affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by the affine-scheme lemma. Write $X=\varprojlim_iX_i$ over $Y$, with each $X_i\to Y$ proper and finitely presented and all transitions and projections $a_i:X\to X_i$ closed immersions. Apply the fibre-dimension limit lemma to the constant base system $Y$: it provides an index $i$ such that every fibre of $X_i\to Y$ has dimension at most $d$. Its comparison maps are precisely the given closed immersions. For the given $F$, $a_{i,*}F$ is quasi-coherent, because a closed immersion is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Affine-morphism cohomology gives $H^p(X_i,a_{i,*}F)\cong H^p(X,F)$. Thus it remains to prove cohomology vanishing for proper finitely presented morphisms over an affine base, with arbitrary quasi-coherent coefficients.

Now assume $f$ finitely presented. Express $Y=\operatorname{Spec}A$ as the inverse limit of spectra of finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-subalgebras of $A$. These form a small nonempty directed set (the subalgebra generated by the union of two finite sets is an upper bound). Apply proper Noetherian-stage descent to obtain a proper finitely presented model $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ whose pullback is $f$. Above this stage take its base changes $f_j:X_j\to Y_j$. They remain proper, and their comparison morphisms are isomorphisms, hence closed immersions. The system has limit $f$: a compatible map into its pullbacks is uniquely the pair of a map into $X_0$ and a compatible family into the $Y_j$, by the fibre-product universal property. The fibre-dimension limit lemma supplies a stage $j$ with all fibres of $f_j$ of dimension at most $d$. The affine $Y_j$ is Noetherian, being of finite type over $\mathbf Z$. The projection $h:X\to X_j$ is affine, as the base change of the morphism $Y\to Y_j$ between affine schemes: use the single-open cover $Y_j$ in the affine-local-target criterion. Therefore $h_*F$ is quasi-coherent and $H^p(X,F)\cong H^p(X_j,h_*F)$. It suffices to prove the assertion over an affine Noetherian base.

Let $f:X\to Y$ now be proper with $Y$ affine Noetherian and fibres of dimension at most $d$. Then $X$ is Noetherian by finite-type permanence, and it is quasi-separated by separatedness over the affine base. Express $F$ as a directed colimit of finitely presented module sheaves $F_\lambda$. A finite presentation is a quotient of a finite free module, hence is of finite type; it is quasi-coherent by the finite-presentation lemma, and therefore coherent by the locally Noetherian coherence criterion. The cohomology-colimit theorem applies to $X$: its affine opens form a basis, and its Noetherian topology makes every open quasi-compact. For completeness the latter topology follows from a finite cover by spectra of Noetherian rings: a descending sequence of closed sets stabilizes on each member, hence globally after the maximum of the finitely many stabilization indices. Thus $H^p(X,F)=\varinjlim_\lambda H^p(X,F_\lambda)$. It remains to prove cohomology vanishing for coherent coefficients.

Fix a coherent $F$, $p>d$, and $y\in Y$. Use the infinitesimal fibres $X_n$ and pullbacks $F_n$ of the formal-functions stalk theorem, with $n\ge1$ and $A_y=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$. The fibre $X_y$ is proper, hence finite type, over the field $\kappa(y)$ and is Noetherian. It has a finite cover by spectra of Noetherian rings; those spaces are Noetherian, and the finite-cover stabilization argument of step 4 proves that $|X_y|$ is Noetherian. On $X_n$ the ideal generated by $\mathfrak m_y$ has $n$th power zero, and its quotient defines $X_y$. Every prime contains every nilpotent element, so on each affine chart passing to this quotient preserves the prime spectrum and its closed sets. These identifications agree on overlaps, yielding $|X_n|\cong|X_y|$. Hence $|X_n|$ is Noetherian of dimension at most $d$. Topological Grothendieck vanishing applied to the underlying abelian sheaf of $F_n$ gives zero cohomology in degree $p$. The module/abelian cohomology comparison, applied with the whole open $X_n$, gives $H^p(X_n,F_n)=0$. This includes empty fibres.

source.place: Tag 0E7D, lemma-higher-direct-images-zero-above-dimension-fibre, last paragraph, expanded proof of coherent.tex Tag 02V7 using 02UZ

proof.text: Put $M=(R^pf_*F)_y$. The formal-functions stalk theorem identifies its completion with $\varprojlim_n H^p(X_n,F_n)$, which is zero by step 5. Proper coherent direct image makes $R^pf_*F$ coherent, so its finite-type stalk $M$ is finitely generated over the Noetherian local ring $A_y$. If $m\in M$, its image in the zero completion is zero, so $m\in\mathfrak m_y^nM$ for every $n$ (these are exactly the kernels of the quotient coordinates of the completion). Krull intersection, applied to $\mathfrak m_y$, which is the Jacobson radical of this local ring, gives $m=0$. Thus $M=0$ for every $y$. The zero-stalk criterion yields $R^pf_*F=0$. The affine-base sections/cohomology comparison then yields $H^p(X,F)=0$ for coherent $F$.

source.place: Tag 0E7D, lemma-higher-direct-images-zero-above-dimension-fibre, last paragraph, coherent.tex Tag 02V7; algebra.tex Tag 00IQ(2) in place of 00DV

proof.text: For arbitrary quasi-coherent $F$ in the Noetherian case, step 4 identifies its degree-$p$ cohomology with a directed colimit whose terms vanish by steps 5--6. Such a colimit is zero: every class has a representative in a zero term. Step 3 transports this vanishing to every proper finitely presented morphism over an affine base, and step 2 to every proper morphism over an affine base. Finally step 1 identifies the sections of $R^pf_*F$ over each affine open with the zero cohomology group and identifies the quasi-coherent restriction with the sheaf associated to its zero module of sections. Thus these restrictions, and hence $R^pf_*F$, are zero. No flatness hypothesis was used, and Noetherian hypotheses occurred only on intermediate models. The case $Y=\varnothing$ is immediate, and $d=0$ is covered by the same argument for every $p>0$.

Step 1 reduces to an affine base with open restriction, 01XK sections and the tilde counit (3); a proper morphism is separated and quasi-compact, as that needs. Step 2 uses 09ZR (an affine Y is qcqs) and the 05M5 node on the constant base system: identity transitions are affine and the comparisons are the closed-immersion transitions; it then uses the affine pushforward and the edge isomorphism. Step 3 uses the Nagata affine Noetherian approximation, the 0A0P cartesian stage (finitely presented = lfp+qc+qs) and base changes over a cofinal index set whose limit is X; 05M5 again, and h is affine because Y->Y_j is affine (01S8 with a single-set cover). Step 4 has X Noetherian and qs; 01PK fp modules are qcoh (0) and of finite type, so coherent by 01XZ; the hypotheses of 01FF hold because X is a Noetherian space. Step 5 has |X_n|=|X_y| (nilpotent ideal), dimension at most d, then 02UZ and the module/abelian comparison. Step 6: the 02OD completion is zero, R^p f_* F is coherent by 02O5 so the stalk is finitely generated, and Krull intersection with m_y gives M=0; zero stalks then give vanishing.
